recommendation: Keep the audit commit. Do not restore the 2018 entered-in-error wording unless Pharmacy reopens or reverses FHIR-54903; future MedicationStatement status work should begin from the later FHIR-32060/FHIR-39271 status-adherence model.
issue_request: FHIR-13978 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification Pharmacy issue for STU3 asking to clarify MedicationRequest and MedicationStatement entered-in-error status definitions, including that medication actions may already have occurred and CDS should account for the status, and to clarify stopped should not be used when the original order or statement was entered in error.
initial_application: Jira records the issue as applied on 2018-02-16 by e4206a3abafba1275c89a32c29f2715a17e0e0e7/build@13084. That commit changed the then-active MedicationRequest and MedicationStatement spreadsheets to add the requested entered-in-error and stopped wording before later terminology/source refactors split those definitions into current CodeSystem XML files.
additional_context: MedicationRequest and MedicationStatement are active current-build resources. Current MedicationRequest still has the stopped caveat and places the CDS guidance on MedicationRequest.status rather than on entered-in-error. FHIR-54903 later explicitly changed both entered-in-error definitions to concise invalid-resource definitions. FHIR-32060 and FHIR-39271 later redesigned MedicationStatement.status so it is about recording status only, with taking/not-taking concepts such as stopped carried by MedicationStatement.adherence.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Reintroducing the FHIR-13978 long entered-in-error text or a MedicationStatement stopped status definition would conflict with later final Pharmacy decisions.

related_jiras.note: Later Applied/Persuasive Pharmacy issue intentionally replaced the long MedicationStatement and MedicationRequest entered-in-error definitions with concise invalid-resource definitions.
Redesigned MedicationStatement status to recorded, entered-in-error, and draft, shifting medication-taking state out of status.
Retained the MedicationStatement status/adherence split after the MedicationStatement rename-back and is already represented on the combined branch.
Later MedicationRequest decision moved CDS guidance away from the entered-in-error code definition and onto the MedicationRequest.status element comment.
